comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PREMISE RE-VERIFIED against run 31535962079 raw log — the 'benign noise' reading is REFUTED. 'command cancelled' is not noise: it is a silently miscounted FAILURE.

DECISIVE EVIDENCE (run 31535962079):
  - occurrences of 'ACLI stderr: X Error: command cancelled' = 15
  - sum of every links_applied= across the whole pass          = 15
  - occurrences of 'update_one: ... failed'                    = 0

The correspondence is exact and per-ticket, not just in aggregate:
  2 cancellations -> REB-1305 links_applied=2; 1 -> REB-1308 links_applied=1;
  2 -> REB-1398 links_applied=2; 2 -> REB-1442 links_applied=2; 1 -> REB-1538/1656/1666
  links_applied=1; 2 -> REB-1694 links_applied=2; 1 -> REB-184/2114/2321 links_applied=1.
Every ticket with zero cancellations reports links_applied=0.

MECHANISM (dispatch_one.py:778-789, _update_one_dispatch_links):

    try:
        _call_with_retry(client.delete_issue_link, link_id)
        _links_applied += 1
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
        # ...treated as idempotent 404/409...
        _links_applied += 1

That arm has NO print, which is exactly why zero 'update_one: ... failed' lines appear: the
generic except-Exception arms never fire. The only trace a cancelled delete leaves is
_run_acli's retry-exhausted 'ACLI stderr:' print (acli_subprocess.py:449-451). The arm then
counts the failure as an applied link.

So links_applied=N in these runs is entirely FABRICATED FROM FAILURES. Zero links were
actually removed in that pass, and batch_outcome reported error=None with a nonzero
links_applied for every one. This is the bug 44de silent-divergence class, and it is why
REBAR_RECONCILER_FAIL_SILENT_NOOP cannot catch it: the canary tests computed>0 and applied==0,
and this arm inflates applied to equal computed.

It is correctly NON-TERMINATING (stinkpot is right that it killed zero runs; those 6 died
later in git delivery). But the code comment justifying the arm — 'self-healing, the differ
recomputes the REMOVE from managed_refs next pass' — does not hold here: the cause is
DETERMINISTIC (EOF on stdin at a confirmation prompt, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL), so every
future pass cancels identically. The links are never removed and every pass reports success.
That is permanent silent divergence, not transient noise.

ROOT CAUSE now has same-repo prior art (surfaced by the plan reviewer, verified): acli.py:714-724
already passes --yes to 'workitem delete' because 'without it, acli jira workitem delete waits
on stdin for confirmation and exits non-zero in non-TTY contexts (bug 3256-f960-4ae6-4943,
surfaced by the live cfd6 capability probe)'. That is the IDENTICAL failure mode. 'link create'
and 'link delete' pass neither --json nor --yes. The ticket's original caution conflated --yes
with --json: story 25ae proved --json is rejected on those subcommands; it says nothing about
--yes, which is proven-accepted on a sibling subcommand.

VERDICT: not_a_bug is wrong; pure log-labelling is insufficient (labelling a fabricated
success as 'benign' would harden the lie). Awaiting coordinator direction on scope.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ITEM 2 VERIFICATION — `--yes` IS accepted on BOTH link subcommands. Verified directly against
the subcommands themselves (not inferred from the `workitem delete` sibling), per the 25ae
lesson that a sibling's flag support proves nothing.

Local binary is `acli version 1.3.19-stable` — the EXACT version the fleet caches
(`acli-Linux-1.3.19-stable` in the bridge workflow), so this is same-version evidence, not a
newer-build guess.

    $ acli jira workitem link create --help
          --yes                Confirm link creation without prompting

    $ acli jira workitem link delete --help
          --yes                Confirm link deletion without prompting

Both subcommands prompt for confirmation by default and both accept `--yes` to skip it. With
`stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` (acli_subprocess.py) that prompt reads EOF and the Go CLI reports
`X Error: command cancelled` — which is exactly the observed string, and exactly the mechanism
bug 3256/cfd6 already documented for `workitem delete`.

Note the asymmetry that misled the original ticket: `--json` is genuinely rejected on these two
subcommands (story 25ae, correct), but `--yes` is genuinely accepted. The two flags had to be
checked separately; conflating them is what produced the "verify before adding" caution.

Root cause is therefore CONFIRMED, not merely suspected: the missing `--yes` causes the
cancellation, and the no-print `except CalledProcessError: _links_applied += 1` arm in
dispatch_one.py converts that cancellation into a reported success.

Proceeding with both approved items.

The reviewer blocked on `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_capability_guard_a3fa.py` unpacking

repo, two different trees — I verified against the wrong one.

It surfaced exactly as the reviewer predicted, on the full suite:

    tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_capability_guard_a3fa.py:186: ValueError:
    too many values to unpack (expected 2)

Both call sites (lines 186 and 264) are now updated to the 3-tuple, and the second one —
"a real link failure MUST still feed the silent-no-op canary" — now also asserts
`failed == 1`, which is the counter that distinguishes it from the designed capability skip

comments.body:
UPDATE to the pause state above: the in-flight review-plan finished while I was recording,
and it returned BLOCK, not PASS. So no attestation was signed, `--status` still reports
`stale-material`, and the push precondition remains UNMET. Still not pushing. ps4 is now
blocked on a code change, not just a signature refresh.

THE FINDING IS CORRECT — I verified the citation in source before accepting it (the inverse
of my earlier mistake, where I dismissed a real finding after checking the wrong tree).

Reviewer's claim: my narrowed idempotent check reads stderr only, but the sibling precedent
it is modelled on matches BOTH streams. Confirmed at
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py:739-742, in delete_issue:

    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
        err_text = (exc.stderr or "") + (exc.stdout or "")
        if "404" in err_text or "not found" in err_text.lower():
            # Already deleted — idempotent success
            return {"status": "not_found", "key": jira_key}

Mine (`_is_idempotent_link_removal`) only inspects `exc.stderr`.

WHY IT MATTERS, and it is the same class of bug as the one being fixed. `link delete` runs
WITHOUT `--json` (story 25ae: ACLI rejects that flag there), so its failure output is
human-readable text on the exit-code path, and a "404 / not found" message can land on
STDOUT rather than stderr. A stderr-only test would then classify a GENUINE concurrent-
removal race as a failure: `links_failed` inflates, and under
REBAR_RECONCILER_FAIL_SILENT_NOOP=1 the canary could fire on a benign race. That is a false
alarm in the honest-counter direction — less dangerous than the silent-success defect this
ticket fixes, but it would erode trust in the very counter being added, which is the whole
point of the change.

THE FIX (small, one function plus coverage), for the resumption:
1. `_is_idempotent_link_removal` in dispatch_apply_phases.py takes the CalledProcessError
   (or both streams) rather than `stderr`, and matches
   `(exc.stderr or "") + (exc.stdout or "")`, citing acli.py:739 as the precedent.
2. Add a case to tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_outbound_link_failure_accounting.py:
   a delete failing with the 404 marker on STDOUT and empty stderr must count
   `links_applied=1, links_failed=0`. That oracle fails against the current stderr-only
   implementation, so it pins the finding rather than restating it.
3. Keep "absent from BOTH streams is not idempotent" — that part of the narrowing stands and
   is what makes the stderr-less regression test meaningful.
4. THEN re-run review-plan (expect PASS), verify `--status` is certified, and only then push
   ps4. Do not touch description/file_impact after the review — that ordering trap already
   cost two CI cycles.

Note the fix does NOT change the ticket's file_impact: dispatch_apply_phases.py and that test
file are both already declared, so step 4 needs no plan edit.

All local gates remain green on b20afb53b3; this finding is about correctness under a stdout-
carried 404, which no current test exercises.

compiled_state.description:
From sole-curbable-stinkpot (9a71-ba9b-89d0-4cb8). The original framing understated this:
the string is not swallowed noise, it is a FAILURE COUNTED AS A SUCCESS. Re-scoped.

## Context / Problem

In the outbound link-apply loop, a cancelled ACLI link delete is counted as an applied link,
so `RECON: batch_outcome ... error=None links_applied=N` reports work that never happened and
the silent-noop canary is blind to it by construction.

Evidence, run 31535962079 raw log:

- `ACLI stderr: X Error: command cancelled` occurrences = 15
- sum of every `links_applied=` across the whole pass    = 15
- occurrences of `update_one: ... failed`                = 0

Exact 1:1 per-ticket, not just in aggregate. Zero links were actually removed that pass.

Mechanism, `_update_one_dispatch_links`: the delete's `except subprocess.CalledProcessError`
arm did `_links_applied += 1`, treating ANY ACLI failure as an idempotent 404/409 race. That
arm has NO print, which is why no `update_one: ... failed` lines appear and why this looked
like free-floating noise. Its rationale ("self-healing — the differ recomputes the REMOVE next
pass") does not hold: the cause is DETERMINISTIC. `link create`/`link delete` prompt for
confirmation and run with `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL`, so the prompt reads EOF and ACLI reports
`command cancelled` every pass, forever. This is the bug 44de silent-divergence class, and
`REBAR_RECONCILER_FAIL_SILENT_NOOP` cannot catch it: the canary tests
`computed > 0 and applied == 0`, and this arm inflates `applied` to equal `computed`.

Root cause CONFIRMED (see ticket comment): `acli 1.3.19-stable` — the version the fleet
caches — documents `--yes` on BOTH subcommands, and neither call site passes it. Verified on
the link subcommands themselves, not inferred from the `workitem delete` sibling. `--json` IS
rejected there (25ae, correct); `--yes` is accepted. Conflating the flags produced the
original "verify before adding" caution.

## Approach

Two edits: stop the lie, then remove its cause.

**1. Stop counting failures as applied** (`dispatch_one.py`). Add a `_links_failed` counter.
The delete handler's `except subprocess.CalledProcessError` arm keeps its idempotent rationale
but narrows to genuine idempotent signatures — `404`, `409`, `does not exist` or `not found`,
case-insensitive, matched across `(stderr or "") + (stdout or "")`. Both streams, per the
`delete_issue` precedent at `adapters/jira/acli.py:739`: `link delete` runs without `--json`,
so its failure text is human-readable on the exit-code path and the marker can land on
STDOUT. Output carrying NO marker is not idempotent. Those still count toward
`_links_applied`, so a benign concurrent removal does not become a new hard failure. Every
other `CalledProcessError` increments `_links_failed` and prints, as does the trailing
`except Exception` arm and the `set_relationship` handler. Every arm stays non-fatal.
`links_failed` rides the existing `subop` dict through `apply_handlers.py` onto the outcome
and is printed in the `batch_outcome` line — an additive field. This alone lets the canary
fire.

**2. Remove the cause** (`acli_graph.py`). Pass `--yes` to both link subcommands, citing the
1.3.19-stable help verification and mirroring the `workitem delete` precedent at
`acli.py:714-724` (bug 3256 / live cfd6 probe).

**Deliberately NOT doing:** no cancellation fast-abort / typed error — with `--yes` removing
the prompt that is speculative machinery, and edit 1 makes any residual failure visible.

**Disjointness.** OUTBOUND ACLI path only: no shared edit region with change 1640's
`_AUTH_FAILURE_MARKERS` / `AcliAuthError` or with the inbound-links state work.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py` — `_links_failed`; narrowed idempotent
  arm; create-side failure counting. `_update_one_dispatch_links` becomes
  `(computed, applied, failed)`; that arity change is contained to one production caller plus
  two call sites in `test_capability_guard_a3fa.py`, all updated. Two size gates bite and are
  handled rather than blessed: the REMOVE sub-phase is extracted into `_dispatch_link_removes`
  along the ADD/REMOVE seam (the narrowed arm puts the parent one over its LOCKED complexity
  ceiling of 17), and the link phase then moves to the sibling leaf below, since
  `dispatch_one.py` crosses the 800-LOC cap.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_apply_phases.py` — receives the link-dispatch
  cluster. The existing seam, not an arbitrary slice: the phase already calls four helpers
  living there, so the move REMOVES cross-module reach and lands beside its sibling
  `_update_one_dispatch_comments`. `dispatch_one` re-imports it, so `dispatch_one.<name>`
  access is unchanged.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_handlers.py` — carry `links_failed` onto outcome.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py` — print `links_failed` in `batch_outcome`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_graph.py` — `--yes` on both link cmds.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_outbound_link_failure_accounting.py` (new).
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_capability_guard_a3fa.py` — unpacks the phase at two call
  sites; updated to the 3-tuple, its real-failure case now also asserting `failed == 1`,
  separating it from the designed capability skip beside it.
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` — the extraction drops the link phase under C901, so its
  entry goes STALE; removed via `--update-stale`. A removal is an improvement, so the lock
  gate still passes (it forbids only raised ceilings and new entries).
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_link_removal_sync.py` — its
  `test_update_one_tolerates_acli_delete_failure` asserts `links_applied == 1` for a
  `CalledProcessError` with **no output**; that ENCODES the defect and flips to
  `links_applied == 0, links_failed == 1`. Its real intent ("does not raise, pass not
  unwound") is preserved, and a `404` sibling keeps idempotent-race coverage.

## Testing

- Happy path: a create + delete that both succeed report `links_applied=2 links_failed=0`.
- Regression (the defect): a `delete_issue_link` raising `CalledProcessError` with
  `command cancelled` stderr yields `links_applied=0 links_failed=1`, not `links_applied=1`.
- Idempotent preserved: the same failure with a `404` marker still counts applied, on
  EITHER stream — a stdout-carried `404` with empty stderr is the stream-coverage oracle.
- No marker on either stream is not idempotent: `stderr=None` counts failed.
- Edge: `set_relationship` failure increments `links_failed`, returns normally (non-fatal).
- Argv: both link argvs contain `--yes` and still no `--json`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A cancelled `delete_issue_link` (non-idempotent stderr) no longer increments
      `links_applied` — verified by a test asserting `links_applied=0, links_failed=1`.
- [x] A failed `delete_issue_link` with an idempotent marker (404/409/does-not-exist/
      not-found) on EITHER stream still counts applied — verified by tests asserting
      `links_applied=1, links_failed=0` for the marker on stderr and again on stdout.
- [x] `CalledProcessError` with no marker on either stream counts failed — verified by test.
- [x] A failed `set_relationship` increments `links_failed` and does not unwind the pass —
      verified by a test asserting `links_applied=0, links_failed=1` and normal return.
- [x] The `RECON: batch_outcome` line for an `update` includes `links_failed=<n>` — verified
      by a test capturing stderr and asserting the substring.
- [x] `workitem link create` and `workitem link delete` argv both include `--yes` — verified
      by a test asserting the flag is present in each command list.
- [x] `test_update_one_tolerates_acli_delete_failure` still asserts `update_one` does not
      raise, its count corrected to `links_applied == 0, links_failed == 1`.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the reconciler unit suite pass.

file_impact.reason: links_failed counter; narrow the idempotent arm; extract the REMOVE sub-phase; hand the link phase to the sibling leaf to stay under the 800-LOC cap
receives the link-dispatch cluster, beside its sibling comment phase and the four helpers it already calls
print links_failed in the batch_outcome line
pass --yes to workitem link create/delete to stop the EOF-on-stdin cancellation
the extraction drops the link phase under C901, so its entry goes stale; removed via --update-stale
new: links_failed accounting, cancellation regression, --yes argv
delete-failure test encoded the defect; flipped, plus a 404 idempotent sibling
unpacks the phase; updated to the 3-tuple and asserts failed==1 separates a real failure from a designed skip
